accepted.s: Which soil is the most extensive soil type in Andhra Pradesh, covering approximately 60–66 per cent of the State’s area?
accepted.x: Red soil is the most extensive soil type in Andhra Pradesh and covers approximately 60–66 per cent of the State’s area.
accepted.tq: Use the distinctive percentage and rank to identify the correct soil type.
accepted.sec: Red soils - share of state area and sub-types

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding red soils of Andhra Pradesh:
1. They are formed mainly from weathered granite, gneiss, Dharwar schists and greenstones.
2. Their red colour is mainly due to ferric oxides.
3. They have high moisture-retention capacity.
4. They are generally poor in nitrogen, phosphorus and organic matter.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is false because red soils have low moisture-retention capacity.
accepted.tq: Find the incorrect soil-property statement by checking the reversed moisture-retention comparison.
accepted.sec: Red soils - share of state area and sub-types

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a crop group commonly associated with the red soils of Andhra Pradesh?
o: Pulses such as red gram and green gram
accepted.x: Red soils of Andhra Pradesh support pulses, groundnut, castor and millets. Tea and rubber are not listed as characteristic crops of these soils.
accepted.tq: Identify the odd crop group by eliminating the crops associated with red soils.
accepted.sec: Red soils - share of state area and sub-types

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below the lists:

List-I (Red-soil sub-type)
A. Red earth with loamy subsoil
B. Red soil with clay base
C. Red loamy soil
D. Red sandy soil

List-II (Share of State area)
1. 30 per cent
2. 12 per cent
3. 9 per cent

Codes:
accepted.x: Red earth with loamy subsoil accounts for 30 per cent, red soil with clay base for 12 per cent, red loamy soil for 9 per cent and red sandy soil for 8 per cent.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure percentage pair and eliminate codes containing a mismatched sub-type.
accepted.sec: Red soils - share of state area and sub-types

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched with reference to the distribution of red soils in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Rayalaseema — Anantapur, Sri Sathya Sai, Kadapa, Nandyal and Kurnool
Konaseema — principal red-soil tract of the State
Godavari delta — exclusive concentration of red soils
accepted.x: Red soils are widely distributed in Rayalaseema, including Anantapur, Sri Sathya Sai, Kadapa, Nandyal and Kurnool, and also occur in coastal uplands.
accepted.tq: Test the location by matching the soil with its principal regional cluster.
accepted.sec: Red soils - share of state area and sub-types

accepted.s: Which one of the following is the correct descending order of the principal soil types of Andhra Pradesh by area coverage?
accepted.x: The principal order is red soil, black soil, deltaic alluvial soil and laterite soil. Their approximate shares are 60–66 per cent, 25 per cent, 5–6 per cent and 1 per cent respectively.
accepted.tq: Arrange the soil categories using both rank and approximate area share.
accepted.sec: Soil types of AP → area ranking and regions

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the distribution of black soils in Andhra Pradesh:
1. Black soil is the second-largest soil group in the State.
2. It is found in districts such as Kurnool, Nandyal, YSR Kadapa, Guntur, Bapatla, Prakasam and Palnadu.
3. It covers approximately 25 per cent of the State’s area.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Black or regur soil is the second-largest soil group in Andhra Pradesh and covers about 25 per cent of the State.
accepted.tq: Accept the complete set when rank, distribution and percentage consistently describe the same soil group.
accepted.sec: Soil types of AP → area ranking and regions

accepted.s:
The deltaic alluvial soils of Andhra Pradesh are principally associated with which of the following regions?
1. Godavari–Krishna deltas
2. Konaseema
3. Nellore
4. Guntur
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Godavari–Krishna deltas, Konaseema, Nellore and Guntur are all listed among the principal areas of deltaic alluvial soils.
accepted.tq: Test a regional distribution list through the coded combination of all valid locations.
accepted.sec: Soil types of AP → area ranking and regions

accepted.s: Which one of the following soil categories is described as occurring in minor amounts in heavily eroded tracts of Andhra Pradesh?
accepted.x: Skeletal soils occur in minor amounts, particularly in heavily eroded tracts of Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Use the distinctive association between a soil category and heavily eroded terrain.
accepted.sec: Soil types of AP → area ranking and regions

accepted.s:
With reference to the Andhra Pradesh Soil Survey and Soil Resources classification for 2024–25, consider the following statements:
1. It recognises 22 soil categories.
2. Ten categories are predominant and together cover more than 88 per cent of the State.
3. Loamy to clayey skeletal deep reddish-brown soils form the largest single category, at 20.42 per cent.
4. Clayey to gravelly clayey moderately deep dark-brown soils account for 18.65 per cent.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. The classification records 22 categories; 10 predominant categories cover more than 88 per cent, with the two stated categories accounting for 20.42 and 18.65 per cent respectively.
accepted.tq: Check each numerical statement independently before selecting the complete coded combination.
accepted.sec: Soil types of AP → area ranking and regions

accepted.s: Which one of the following is the correct order of the three largest individual soil categories under the Andhra Pradesh Soil Survey and Soil Resources classification?
o: Moderately deep calcareous black; loamy to clayey skeletal deep reddish-brown; clayey to gravelly clayey moderately deep dark-brown
Loamy to clayey skeletal deep reddish-brown; clayey to gravelly clayey moderately deep dark-brown; moderately deep calcareous black
Clayey to gravelly clayey moderately deep dark-brown; moderately deep calcareous black; loamy to clayey skeletal deep reddish-brown
Clayey to gravelly clayey moderately deep dark-brown; loamy to clayey skeletal deep reddish-brown; moderately deep calcareous black
accepted.x: The three largest categories are loamy to clayey skeletal deep reddish-brown soils at 20.42 per cent, clayey to gravelly clayey moderately deep dark-brown soils at 18.65 per cent, and moderately deep calcareous black soils at 9.57 per cent.
accepted.tq: Compare the stated percentages and arrange the categories in descending order.
accepted.sec: Soil types of AP → area ranking and regions

accepted.s: Which one of the following soil categories has the smallest share among the categories specifically listed under the Andhra Pradesh Soil Survey and Soil Resources classification?
o: Clayey to gravelly clayey moderately deep dark-brown soils
Loamy to clayey skeletal deep reddish-brown soils
accepted.x: Clayey moderately deep wet soils are the smallest specifically listed category, with a share of 0.13 per cent.
accepted.tq: Identify the minimum by comparing the stated category percentages.
accepted.sec: Soil types of AP → area ranking and regions

accepted.s: Fertile land in Andhra Pradesh is particularly associated with the valleys and plains of which set of rivers?
o: Tungabhadra, Musi, Nagavali and Bahuda only
accepted.x: Fertile land in Andhra Pradesh lies along the Krishna, Godavari, Penna and Vamsadhara river systems.
accepted.tq: Recall the complete river set associated with fertile land in the State.
accepted.sec: Soil types of AP → area ranking and regions

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements correctly describes the geological base underlying much of Andhra Pradesh?
o: It is entirely underlain by recent deltaic deposits.
It is predominantly underlain by granitoid-gneiss bedrock.
It is predominantly underlain by basaltic lava flows.
It is chiefly underlain by unconsolidated marine sediments.
accepted.x: Granitoid-gneiss bedrock underlies much of Andhra Pradesh, although several other formations and deposited soils also occur.
accepted.tq: Use the precise geological description rather than an extreme statement about the whole State.
accepted.sec: Soil types of AP → area ranking and regions

accepted.s: Laterite soils in Andhra Pradesh cover approximately what proportion of the State’s area?
accepted.x: Laterite soils constitute approximately 1 per cent of the area of Andhra Pradesh and occur mainly in coastal pockets and hills.
accepted.tq: Use the distinctive small percentage to distinguish laterite from the major soil groups.
accepted.sec: Laterite soils in AP - extent, formation, areas

accepted.s:
Assertion (A): Laterite soils are generally acidic and have low fertility in Andhra Pradesh.
Reason (R): Intense leaching under conditions of high temperature and heavy rainfall removes silica and lime from the soil.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
accepted.x: Both statements are true. Intense leaching removes silica and lime, contributing to acidity and low fertility in laterite soils.
accepted.tq: Test whether the stated formation process directly explains the soil properties.
accepted.sec: Laterite soils in AP - extent, formation, areas

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the formation of laterite soils in Andhra Pradesh is INCORRECT?
o: Silica and lime are leached from the soil during their formation.
They are formed mainly in semi-arid regions receiving low rainfall.
High temperature and heavy rainfall favour their formation.
accepted.x: Laterite soils form under high temperature and heavy rainfall through intense leaching. Formation in semi-arid, low-rainfall regions is incorrect.
accepted.tq: Spot the reversed climatic condition in the soil-formation statement.
accepted.sec: Laterite soils in AP - extent, formation, areas

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about laterite soils of Andhra Pradesh:
1. They are generally red to yellowish-red.
2. They are well drained.
3. They are rich in hydrated iron and aluminium oxides.
4. They are highly fertile because of abundant nitrogen and organic matter.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false because laterite soils are generally less fertile and poor in organic matter; their fertility is low despite the presence of iron and aluminium oxides.
accepted.tq: Reject the exaggerated fertility claim while retaining the colour, drainage and oxide properties.
accepted.sec: Laterite soils in AP - extent, formation, areas

accepted.s: Which one of the following groups consists entirely of areas associated with laterite soils in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Anantapur, Sri Sathya Sai, Kadapa and Nandyal only
Kurnool, Nandyal, Palnadu, Bapatla and Guntur
Ellavaram, Peddapuram, Kavali, Kovvur, Gudur and Sullurpeta
Konaseema, Krishna delta, Godavari delta and Nellore delta
accepted.x: Ellavaram, Peddapuram, Kavali, Kovvur, Gudur and Sullurpeta are listed as laterite-soil areas. Laterite also occurs in elevated areas such as Satyavedu and Puttur and in coastal pockets.
accepted.tq: Check whether every location in the option belongs to the same soil-distribution group.
accepted.sec: Laterite soils in AP - extent, formation, areas

accepted.s: The North Coastal agro-climatic zone of Andhra Pradesh is characteristically associated with which soil?
accepted.x: The North Coastal agro-climatic zone is characterised by laterite soils.
accepted.tq: Link the agro-climatic zone with its characteristic soil type.
accepted.sec: Laterite soils in AP - extent, formation, areas

1. Mango

3. Plantation crops
4. Tamarind and turmeric
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Laterite soils in Andhra Pradesh support mango, cashew and plantation crops; tamarind and turmeric are also listed among suitable crops.

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: Dubba is a local red-soil sub-type. Khadar denotes new alluvium, Chalka denotes red sandy soil, and Regadi denotes black cotton soil.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between closely related local soil names and their meanings.

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs correctly represents the two forms of alluvium mentioned in relation to soil names?
accepted.x: Bhangar refers to old alluvium, whereas Khadar refers to new alluvium.
